extracted.intended_audience: researchers (PIs), co-PIs, and institutional sponsored-projects/administrative staff preparing and managing NSF proposals and awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and administering NSF proposals and awards under the PAPPG (NSF 24-1), including formatting, required documents, eligibility, disclosure obligations, merit review criteria, and post-award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with Instructions for Proposal Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must conform with NSF Proposal Preparation and Submission requirements; deviations must be justified and, if necessary, authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes instructions on how to handle deviations, requests for reasonable and accessibility accommodations, and the requirement that proposals follow the format, content, and submission procedures set forth in the PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Format: Font, Spacing, Margin, Pagination, and Landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal font, spacing, margin, and pagination requirements must be followed; submission of proposal documents in landscape format is allowed (per updated guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Proposal Pagination Instructions and Proposal Font, Spacing, and Margin Requirements for specifics (font size, margins, page numbering). Nonconforming proposals may be returned or not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description: Content and Page Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Description must contain required content and adhere to page limitations; inclusion of Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) within the Project Description is governed by PAPPG rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Description must include Results from Prior NSF Support where applicable, address unfunded collaborations and group proposal specifics, and respect any stated page limits and formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Project Summary must be provided as part of the proposal and follow PAPPG content requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary content and structure are prescribed in Chapter II (e.g., may need to address intellectual merit and broader impacts); follow the exemplar and content headings required by NSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual Merit — one of the core NSF merit review criteria assessing the potential to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the intellectual merit of the proposed activity according to the principles in Chapter III; proposals must present clear scholarly/scientific rationale, methods, and potential contributions to knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader Impacts — one of the core NSF merit review criteria assessing the potential to benefit society and contribute to desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must describe broader impacts activities and how the project will benefit broader communities, education, diversity, and societal needs; reviewers evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of these plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF selects reviewers to evaluate proposals according to selection processes described in the PAPPG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conflict-of-interest screening and procedures for choosing appropriate reviewers; see Chapter III for reviewer selection and confidentiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Types and Submission Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals may be submitted as various types: concept outlines, letters of intent (LOIs), preliminary proposals, full proposals, program announcements, solicitations, DCLs, and special categories (e.g., RAPID, EAGER, RAISE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each proposal type has specific preparation and submission rules described in Chapter II.F; proposers must follow the special instructions for the type of submission they are making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Submit Proposals: Eligibility of Organizations and Individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility rules define which organizations and individuals may submit proposals (IHEs, non-profits, for-profits, Tribal Nations, foreign organizations, unaffiliated individuals, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter I.E describes categories of eligible organizations and ineligible individuals (including specific provisions for Tribal Nations and foreign entities). Follow the eligibility definitions carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties to Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Programs — Senior/Key Ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who are party to a Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program are not eligible to serve as a senior/key person on an NSF proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New section incorporated per CHIPS and Science Act requirements; proposers must certify as required and NSF guidance explains applicability to senior/key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Programs (Organization-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must provide a certification regarding organizational responsibilities and compliance related to Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Programs where required by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter II.D.1.d(ix) addresses the organizational certification requirement tied to Section 10632 of the CHIPS and Science Act (42 U.S.C. § 19232). Follow required certification language and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Disclosure Requirements: Preaward and Postaward
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF disclosure requirements include both preaward disclosures and postaward annual reporting obligations (including Foreign Financial Support reporting mandated by CHIPS Act Section 10339B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter II.B details disclosure requirements, reporting timelines, and consequences for violations. Postaward disclosures include annual reporting of foreign financial support and related certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and Pending (Other) Support Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include Current and Pending (Other) Support information following NSF's implementation of the common form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated guidance implements the common form developed by the NSTC Research Security Subcommittee; follow instructions in II.D.2.i(ii) and use the prescribed format and level of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical sketch guidance updated: the 3-page limitation for the biographical sketch has been removed; new format aligns with the common form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synergistic Activities section removed from the biographical sketch and must be provided as part of senior/key personnel documents in Research.gov. Follow the new common-form implementation guidance in II.D.2.h.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring Plan Requirement and Page Limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A mentoring plan is required for postdoctoral researchers or graduate students supported on the project; the mentoring plan page limitation remains one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated to address the America COMPETES Act revision; include a one-page mentoring plan per II.D.2.i(i) that meets the specified content and formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A Data Management and Sharing Plan is a required component of proposals where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a Data Management and Sharing Plan per Chapter II special information requirements (II.D.2.i(ii)), describing how data will be managed and shared consistent with NSF policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects Requiring Advanced Computing, Data, and Analysis Capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that require advanced computing, data, or analysis capabilities must follow revised instructions addressing those resource needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter II.E.7 contains updated instructions for describing required computing resources, access plans, and any support requests for advanced computational capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking and Obtaining Tribal Nation Approval for Projects Impacting Tribal Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that may impact Tribal Nation resources or interests must obtain prior written approval from the official(s) designated by the relevant Tribal Nation(s); without prior written approval, projects will not be awarded by NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New section II.E.10: proposers must secure and document Tribal Nation approval before award; follow the required consultation and documentation procedures exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe and Inclusive Working Environments for Off-Campus / Off-Site Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals and postaward activities involving off-site or off-campus research must address plans for safe and inclusive working environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter II and VII revisions (e.g., VII.B.6) require consideration and documentation of safety/inclusion plans for off-site research; include relevant risk mitigation and supervision plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects Involving Human Subjects, Vertebrate Animals, Hazardous Materials, or Endangered Species
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals involving human subjects, live vertebrate animals, hazardous materials, endangered species, or similar regulated activities must include required documentation and approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the necessary protocols, IRB/IACUC approvals, hazard plans, and any required environmental or regulatory documentation per II.D.2.i and II.E subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Environmental Statutes and Tribal Consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals subject to federal environmental statutes must follow updated requirements, including consultation with Tribal Nations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter II.D.2.i(iv) updated to address consultation requirements; include environmental compliance documentation as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification: Required Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets must include allowable cost categories and justifications: salaries and wages (including senior/key person policies), fringe benefits, equipment, travel (domestic, foreign, participant support), consultant services, materials and supplies, computer services, subawards, total direct and indirect costs, fees, amount requested, and cost sharing where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter II budget instructions and justification format. Include confidential budgetary information only where permitted and follow NSF policies on administrative/clerical salaries and other specific cost categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and Unallowable Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF specifies allowable and unallowable costs; unallowable categories include certain entertainment costs, alcoholic beverages, and other specific items (including some telecommunications/video surveillance services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See II.D.2.f(xiii) and related sections for specific prohibitions (e.g., entertainment, meals/coffee breaks rules, alcoholic beverages, home office workspace considerations, prohibition on certain telecommunications and video surveillance services or equipment). Ensure requested items comply with policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF prohibits the use of funds for certain telecommunications and video surveillance services or equipment as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult II.D.2.f(xiii)(e) and X.F for the prohibited providers/services and any exceptions; do not include disallowed items in budgets or procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Timing and Local Time Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The 5 p.m. submitter’s local time deadline is tied to the submitting organization, not the location of the PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies what 'local time' means for submission deadlines; proposers must ensure organizational submitter adheres to the relevant time zone and NSF deadline policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements Relating to Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must meet UEI and System for Award Management (SAM) registration requirements for new and renewal proposals and for award transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter I.G.2 updated to clarify the SAM and UEI requirements, timelines for registration, and implications for submission and award processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Certifications and Single-Copy Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain documents and certifications must be submitted as single-copy documents (e.g., list of suggested reviewers or reviewers not to include, proprietary/privileged information, organizational and senior/key personnel certifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow instructions in II.D.1 and Exhibit II-1 for single-copy submissions and required certifications, including submission channels and signature/authorization requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results From Prior NSF Support Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include Results from Prior NSF Support where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required reporting of past NSF-funded activities, outputs, and impacts in the designated section of the proposal (see II.D.2.d(iii)/(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Collaborations Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must disclose unfunded collaborations as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document collaborations that were not funded by NSF but influenced the proposal; follow II.D.2.d(iv) instructions for content and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group and Collaborative Proposal Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Group proposals and collaborative submissions must follow specific formatting and submission procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See II.D.2.d(v) and II.F collaborative proposal guidance for required components, lead organization responsibilities, and subaward/submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Proposal Processing Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain proposals require special processing (e.g., special components in new proposals or supplemental funding requests); follow the special processing instructions in Chapter II and Exhibit II-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes exhibit references and procedural steps for proposals with confidential information, foreign components, or other special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects Requiring Field Plans and Logistical Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals involving fieldwork must include logistical requirements and a field plan addressing safety, permits, and local/regulatory considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See II.D.2.i and II.E sections on field plans, including permits, cultural/resource protections, and coordination with local authorities or Tribal Nations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects Involving Potential Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that may constitute potential life sciences DURC must follow PAPPG guidance and provide required documentation and mitigation plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow II.D.2.i(iv) / II.E DURC guidance, including review, oversight, and specific proposal disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects Requiring Institutional and Postaward Reporting: Annual and Final Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must submit annual and final project reports, including the Project Outcomes Report for the general public and other technical reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VII.D details reporting schedules, required content, public outcomes reporting (POR), and submission procedures. Also includes Foreign Financial Disclosure Report requirements under CHIPS & Science Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Financial Support Reporting (CHIPS & Science Act Section 10339B)
rubrics_metrics.description: New institutional annual reporting requirements mandated by Section 10339B require disclosure of foreign financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VII.D and II.B describe who must report, timelines, and the substance of the required foreign financial support disclosures; noncompliance carries consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Development Plans (IDPs) for Postdoctoral Scholars and Graduate Students
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral scholars and graduate students who receive substantial NSF support must have Individual Development Plans that are updated annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VII.B.7 implements statutory requirements (Section 10313 of CHIPS & Science Act); awardees must maintain and update IDPs annually and make them available as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postaward Additions: Adding Postdoctoral or Graduate Student Researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Postaward procedures for adding postdoctoral scholars and graduate students have been modified and expanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VII.B.5 updated to require additions to cover graduate student researchers as well as postdocs; follow notification and approval processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postaward Addition of Off-Site or Off-Campus Research
rubrics_metrics.description: A new postaward section addresses requirements associated with adding off-site or off-campus research activities after award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VII.B.6 specifies documentation and assurances needed to permit off-site research, including safety and inclusive environment plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of an Award When a PI Transfers Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures govern disposition of awards when a PI transfers from one organization to another, including responsibilities, transfer of funds/equipment, and conditions for transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VII.B.2.f describes steps, roles of originating and receiving organizations, and statutory considerations; follow NSF processes for transfer or change of PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Periods, Start/End Dates, and Extensions (No-Cost and Special Creativity Extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF specifies award periods, start and end dates, no-cost extensions, and two-year extensions for special creativity where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VI.D outlines types of additional funding support and extension policies (including two-year special creativity extensions) and requirements for requesting extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Support Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF may provide supplemental funding opportunities, with possible durations and funding amounts identified in DCLs or solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VI.E updated to reflect that supplement opportunities may be longer than six months and must follow solicitation/DCL terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Financial Management and Payment Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain financial management systems that meet NSF standards and follow payment request procedures, working capital advance rules, and recipient banking information maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VIII details payment requesting procedures, recipient banking info (including updates for postdoctoral fellowship awards to individuals), erroneous payments handling, interest on advances, and program income rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erroneous Payments and Payment Confirmation Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for identifying and resolving erroneous payments (including confirming correct remittance forms) are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VIII.D.2 updated to provide instructions for confirming that correct forms are used and steps to correct erroneous remittances to NSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Standards: Conflict of Interest, Responsible and Ethical Conduct of Research (RECR), Procurement, and Property Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must adhere to recipient standards covering conflicts of interest, responsible conduct of research, procurement procedures, property management, and other institutional responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter IX and related sections outline institutional obligations, COI policies, RECR expectations, procurement standards, and property handling; institutions must implement compliant policies and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Discrimination, Harassment, and Environmental Justice Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF incorporates updated non-discrimination statutes and regulations, including coverage of Executive Order 14096 on Environmental Justice and updates to NSF's policy on sexual harassment and other forms of harassment or sexual assault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XI.A and XI.M include updated language and expectations for institutions; proposers and awardees must be aware of and comply with non-discrimination and environmental justice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Integrity Definition and Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF incorporates a new definition of scientific integrity derived from Federal guidance and sets expectations for responsible scientific practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XI.M implements the framework from the National Science and Technology Council; institutions and investigators must ensure research integrity policies and practices align with these definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Reporting Requirements and Release of Recipient Proposal Information
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF describes technical reporting requirements and the conditions under which recipient proposal information may be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter VII.D and III.B explain what review information is provided to PIs, how recipient proposal information is handled, and the reporting obligations for technical and programmatic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Processing, Review Revisions, and Funding Recommendation Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF procedures govern proposal processing, reviewer evaluation, permissible revisions during review, and the process for funding recommendations and award/decline decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter III and IV describe the review timeline, revision rules, reconsideration and resubmission policies, and how NSF communicates decisions to proposers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Preparation Checklist and Potentially Disqualifying Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal preparation checklist and definitions of potentially disqualifying conflicts of interest are provided to assist proposers in compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist (II.F/II.D exhibits) to ensure completeness; consult the conflict-of-interest guidance to avoid submission problems or reviewer disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Funding Categories and ROA/PUI Supplemental Funding Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: New listing of Research Opportunity Awards for Predominantly Undergraduate Institutions (ROA/PUI) as a supplemental funding request type; other special categories (RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, GOALI, etc.) retain specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific instructions for each special funding category (Chapter II.F and II.C.2) including eligibility, budgets, and submission details for ROA/PUI and other mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation Requirements for International Activities and Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals involving foreign organizations, subawards, or consultants must include clarification and justification for funding foreign entities through NSF budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter I.E and II.D guidance updated to clarify information required from proposers when requesting funding flows to foreign organizations or individuals (through subaward or consultant arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on Subawards and Transferring Part of an NSF Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Subawarding or transferring part of an NSF award requires compliance with PAPPG policies and specific documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See II.D.2.f, VII.B.4, and related sections for subaward policies, procedures, approvals, and financial/administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for Collaborative Arrangements and Letters of Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include documentation of collaborative arrangements and letters of collaboration where needed to demonstrate the significance and nature of collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow II.D.2.i(ii)-(iii) for acceptable forms and content of collaboration documentation and limitations on letters of collaboration vs. formal subawards/consultancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Limit and Content Changes for Biographical Sketch and Senior/Key Personnel Documentation (Synergistic Activities Moved)
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergistic Activities removed from the biographical sketch and must now be submitted as part of senior/key personnel documents in Research.gov; biographical sketch page limit removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Synergistic Activities and other former biographical-sketch content in the senior/key personnel fields as required; follow Research.gov guidance for senior/key personnel documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for Declinations, Reconsideration, and Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF outlines policies for declinations, requests for reconsideration, and resubmission of declined proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter IV covers proposal withdrawal, not accepted/returned without review, declinations, reconsideration procedures, and guidance on resubmitting proposals after declines.
